analysis: The method `norm` trims the input string `resPath` and then enters a loop to remove any leading double slashes, followed by another loop to remove any trailing slashes. After these loops, it ensures the string starts with a slash. The `substring` method is used within these loops. According to the provided documentation, `substring` can throw an `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if `beginIndex` is negative, `endIndex` is larger than the length of the string, or `beginIndex` is larger than `endIndex`. In the code, `substring(1)` and `substring(0, resPath.length() - 1)` are used. The first call `substring(1)` is safe as long as `resPath` is not empty, and the second call `substring(0, resPath.length() - 1)` is safe as long as `resPath` has a length of at least 1. The code does not explicitly check the length of `resPath` before calling `substring`, so if `resPath` is an empty string, the `substring` calls could trigger an `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
remark: The `IndexOutOfBoundsException` can be triggered in the `norm` method if the `resPath` is an empty string. In this case, the `substring(1)` call will attempt to start at an index that is out of bounds (index 1 in an empty string), and the `substring(0, resPath.length() - 1)` call will attempt to end at an index that is out of bounds (index -1 in an empty string).
